metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Kansas (2026): Rules, Exemptions & Examples

description: Kansas has statewide sales tax, but precious-metal bullion and coins are fully exempt when qualifying. Jewelry is taxable. No threshold is required.

What's covered by the exemption
Precious-metal bullion and coins
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Even when the state-level rule is clear, cities or counties in this state may charge their own tax. Here's what to expect.
Local treatment
Local jurisdictions generally follow state exemption
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Kansas.
Is bullion taxable in Kansas?
+
No. Kansas provides a full sales-tax exemption for qualifying precious-metal bullion.
Are gold and silver coins exempt from Kansas sales tax?
+
Yes for qualifying coins under the bullion/coin exemption, while nonqualifying collectibles may still be taxable.
Do I pay sales tax on numismatic coins in Kansas?
+
Sometimes. Kansas exempts qualifying bullion/coins, but collectible pieces that don’t meet the exemption criteria can be taxable.
Is jewelry taxable in Kansas?
+
Yes. Precious-metal jewelry is taxable even though qualifying bullion and coins are exempt.
Can local Kansas taxes remove the bullion exemption?
+
Generally no. Local jurisdictions typically follow the state exemption for qualifying bullion and coins.
